symptom: UPS Automatically Switched into Static Bypass Mode
possibleCauses: Heavy inrush or downstream short-circuit overload
Internal inverter thyristor over-temperature
Inverter DC link voltage out of nominal window
Manual bypass button triggered during unauthorized inspection
diagnosticSteps: Check the LCD touch screen alarm log and record exact timestamp code.
Inspect PDU circuit meters to verify if downstream load exceeded 100% capacity.
Check ambient temperature in UPS battery and converter compartments.
Verify static bypass input utility frequency and voltage stability.
correctiveActions: If caused by temporary load inrush, clear fault on downstream panel and re-engage inverter via control menu.
If internal inverter fault persists, leave in bypass, isolate inverter module, and invoke tier-2 emergency vendor support.
Verify ventilation fan operations inside the UPS cabinet.

symptom: Generator Cranks but Fails to Start during Blackout
possibleCauses: Starting battery bank voltage below 24VDC under load
Fuel supply line airlocked or fuel shut-off solenoid unenergized
Jacket water preheater failed, resulting in cold cylinder failure to combust
Emergency Stop pushbutton physically latched
diagnosticSteps: Measure starter battery terminal voltage during crank attempt (must stay > 20VDC).
Inspect engine fuel shut-off solenoid linkage and fuel day tank level gauge.
Verify emergency stop button status on local engine panel and remote NOC panel.
Check engine jacket water temperature gauge (should read > 40°C on standby).
correctiveActions: Switch to redundant secondary starter battery bank via selector switch.
Prime the diesel fuel lift pump manually and purge air from filtration manifold.
Release emergency stop latch and reset alarm state on Woodward synchronizer.
Follow EOP for manual generator parallel start.

possibleCauses: Chilled water modulating valve stuck in closed/partially closed state
Air filters clogged, severely choking intake CFM airflow
Cold aisle containment sliding door left propped open
Sudden high density compute server rack provisioning without cooling reallocation
diagnosticSteps: Verify supply chilled water differential pressure and temperature at unit header.
Check PAC actuator valve position display (0-100%).
Measure air temperature differential (Delta T) across cooling coil.
Ensure containment door seals and roof panels are tightly closed.
correctiveActions: Manually override 3-way chilled water valve actuator to full open 100%.
Spin up standby redundant PAC unit in the affected server pod.
Replace clogged synthetic air filters immediately.

symptom: Aspirating Pipe Low Airflow Trouble Alarm
possibleCauses: Aspiration sampling pipe cracked or disconnected above false ceiling
Sampling holes clogged with drywall dust or foreign debris
Aspirator motor RPM degradation
Airflow sensor calibration drift
diagnosticSteps: Check individual pipe flow percentage readings on LCD panel (Normal: 100%).
Trace sampling pipe physical run in the affected sector for loose unions.
Check whether maintenance work or drilling occurred in the zone.
Inspect filter cartridge condition in VESDA detector housing.
correctiveActions: Re-seat dislodged PVC pipe couplings using approved solvent.
Blow out sampling pipe using dry nitrogen or filtered low-pressure compressed air.
Replace intake foam filter cartridge if past replacement date.

possibleCauses: Enclosure cooling fans tripped or circuit breaker opened
Harmonic distortion from non-linear server power supply loads
High ambient temperature in substation basement
Phase current unbalance across the three windings
diagnosticSteps: Read RTD PT100 temperature indicators on front controller panel for Phase U, V, and W.
Measure ventilation fan air flow across bottom transformer coils.
Check incoming LV switchgear power quality meter for THD (Total Harmonic Distortion).
Inspect ambient exhaust fan in transformer room.
correctiveActions: Force transformer cooling fans to continuous manual RUN mode.
Balance downstream phase loads across PDU A and PDU B busbars.
Verify substation exhaust louvers are operating at 100% capacity.
If temperature climbs toward 140°C, transfer load to redundant path and isolate.
